statement:
## Refresh temporally activated package-backed references

Implement `refresh_references(initial, snapshots, references)` and return one tuple per reference, in input order:

`(status, namespace, location, hash)`

`status` is `"invalid"`, `"missing"`, or `"located"`.

The initial index is snapshot 0. Applying atomic batch `i` produces snapshot `i`. An entry has `namespace`, `name`, `version`, and nonempty opaque `hash`. An update has the same fields, but `hash=None` deletes its key. A key is `(namespace, name, version)`. Keys are unique within `initial` and within each batch. Namespaces are `"type"`, `"function"`, and `"value"`. Names are canonical dot-separated fully qualified names. Type versions are `None`; function/value versions are `None` or integers.

A reference has `namespace`, `text`, `context`, `location`, `hash`, and `start`. `start` is an integer from 0 through `len(snapshots)`: the reference does not exist before that snapshot and is processed at `start` and every later snapshot. If `location` is `None`, `hash` is also `None`; otherwise both are canonical and nonempty respectively.

Identifiers contain only ASCII letters, digits, or `_`. Module identifiers and function/value terminals start with `a`–`z`; type terminals start with `A`–`Z`. `context` is empty or dot-separated module identifiers.

`text` consists of zero or more module identifiers followed by a terminal. A function/value terminal may end in `@N`, where `N` is `0` or a positive decimal integer without leading zeroes. The suffix supplies the version and is removed from the name; no suffix means `None`. Type terminals cannot contain a suffix. Any violation makes the reference terminally invalid.

An invalid reference returns `("invalid", original_namespace, original_location, original_hash)` and is never processed.

A valid reference already having a location is location-authoritative from its `start` snapshot onward. At each such snapshot, if its exact key exists, its hash becomes the entry’s current hash; otherwise its retained hash is unchanged. It never moves and returns `"located"`.

For a valid location-less reference, form candidates by prepending the longest through shortest prefix of `context` to the qualified parsed name, including the empty prefix. At each snapshot from `start` onward, select the first currently existing candidate. Type and function references search only their namespace. Value references search every value candidate first, then every function candidate; a function match changes the namespace to `"function"`. Once matched, the reference becomes location-authoritative immediately and for all later snapshots. If no snapshot matches, return `("missing", original_namespace, None, None)`.

All non-reference input obeys its canonical rules. There are at most 200,000 snapshots, entries, updates, and references each, and at most 1,000,000 induced candidate names. Use only the standard library, with no I/O or global state.
